title: Alport syndrome and thin basement membrane disease

steps.tx: **Alport syndrome** is caused by pathogenic variants in COL4A5 on chromosome Xq22.3 in 85% of cases (X-linked Alport syndrome), or bi-allelic variants in autosomal COL4A3 or COL4A4 on chromosome 2q36 (autosomal recessive Alport syndrome). The image is type IV collagen triple helix mutations and pedigree in Alport syndrome.

steps.tx: Pathognomonic electron microscopic finding in Alport syndrome is irregular thinning, thickening, splitting, and '**basket-weave**' lamellation of the glomerular basement membrane lamina densa. The paired value for Embryonic network is alpha-1, alpha-1, alpha-2 (IV). The paired value for Mature GBM network is alpha-3, alpha-4, alpha-5 (IV).

steps.tx: **Sensorineural hearing loss** in Alport syndrome is progressive, bilateral, symmetrical, and initially affects high frequencies (2000 to 8000 Hz), sparing conversational frequencies in early childhood. One side is Alport Syndrome, and the other side is Thin BM Disease. A key point is Irregular thick and thin segments.

steps.tx: Pathognomonic ocular signs in Alport syndrome include **anterior lenticonus** (conical protrusion of the anterior lens capsule into the anterior chamber in 25% of cases) and perimacular dot-and-fleck retinopathy that spares the fovea. The paired value for Auditory system is Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural deafness. The paired value for Ocular anterior segment is Bilateral anterior lenticonus.

steps.tx: Early initiation of **ACE inhibitors** (ramipril, enalapril) or ARBs significantly delays onset of end-stage kidney disease and extends life expectancy by decades in both males and females with Alport syndrome. The first step is Random X-inactivation (lyonization) in podocytes. The next step is Mosaic expression of normal and mutant COL4A5.

Segmental capillary wall fragility and microhematuria
Progression to CKD in 15% to 30% of female carriers

steps.tx: **Thin basement membrane nephropathy** (benign familial hematuria) is caused by heterozygous carrier mutations in COL4A3 or COL4A4, displaying diffuse thinning of the GBM (< 200 to 250 nm) with normal lamellation and lifelong preserved renal function. The image is electron microscopy showing diffuse thinning of the glomerular basement membrane.
steps.say: Thin basement membrane nephropathy (benign familial hematuria) is caused by heterozygous carrier mutations in COL4A3 or COL4A4, displaying diffuse thinning of the GBM ( less than 200 to 250 nm) with normal lamellation and lifelong preserved renal function. The image is electron microscopy showing diffuse thinning of the glomerular basement membrane.

vis.alt: Electron microscopy showing diffuse thinning of the glomerular basement membrane
vis.caption: Diffuse uniform thinning of the glomerular lamina densa in benign familial hematuria (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Following kidney transplantation in Alport syndrome, approximately 3% to 5% of patients develop de novo **anti-GBM** crescentic glomerulonephritis directed against the donor allograft's alpha-5 or alpha-3 type IV collagen chains. One side is TBMD (Carrier State), and the other side is Autosomal Recessive Alport.

left.title: TBMD (Carrier State)
points: Normal GFR and absent proteinuria lifelong

right.title: Autosomal Recessive Alport
points: Progression to ESRD in early adulthood

steps.tx: **Diffuse leiomyomatosis** of the esophagus, tracheobronchial tree, and female genitalia occurs in a subset of Alport syndrome cases caused by contiguous gene deletions spanning the adjacent COL4A5 and COL4A6 genes. The first step is Donor kidney expresses normal alpha-5 chain of type IV collagen.
